newsitem.title: USA: Green group has congressional chairmen in sights.
newsitem.headline: Green group has congressional chairmen in sights.

text.p: The Wilderness Society plans to launch a campaign to oust Alaska Republicans Sen. Frank Murkowski and Representative Don Young as heads of the Senate and House resource committees, a spokesman for the group said Wednesday.

The group said it was starting a national petition drive Thursday to press Republican leaders to drop Murkowski as chairman of the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee and Young as chairman of the House Resources Committee.
"These guys clearly don't fit in this strategy of finding common ground" that Republican leaders have been espousing since last week's elections, the spokesman said.

Both men introduced or endorsed a range of legislation that green groups blasted, including moves to open a portion of the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge to oil drilling, limit the scope of the Endangered Species Act and extend logging in Alaska's Tongass Forest.

The Wilderness Society spokesman acknowledged that getting rid of Murkowski and Young as chairmen was "a long shot." But he said the group's effort might force Republican leaders to explain how they could pursue a moderate course with lawmakers like Murkowski and Young in key positions.
